title: Hook a bed's side rail onto its headboard post: both hooks into their slots at once, then drive it down until seated
instruction: Attach the side rail's loose end to the headboard post, fully seated.
context: Taking a wooden bed apart and putting it back together comes with almost every move, and moves are frequent (a US resident can expect to move 11.7 times in a lifetime, US Census Bureau). Many solid-wood beds join rails to posts with hook-in fasteners like this Rockler one: two hooks on the rail's end go through two slots in the post's plate and drop behind it, and their tapered throats wedge the joint, so the rail is tapped down to lock it, as bed makers' instructions say. The rail's far end sits in the footboard; its near end lies on the floor. The hands carry that end (about 19 N) and keep the rail plumb, because both 4 mm hooks must meet their 6.35 mm slots at once and at the right height (a 3.2 mm window) while pressing towards the post; then both drive the joint down its last 3 mm. Lifted only to its seated height and pushed at the post, the rail's hooks meet solid plate and never go in; one arm alone can hang the rail but not drive it home.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights in mm above the table top, which stands in for the bedroom floor. Headboard post: hardwood, 76 x 76 mm, standing on the floor at x 0.262 to 0.338, y 0.070 to 0.146, cropped 212 mm up; its face at y 0.070 faces the robot's right. A stub of the headboard's bottom rail (25 x 165 mm hardwood) runs from the post's far side 220 mm away from the arms (x 0.338 to 0.558, centred on y 0.108, 35 to 200 mm up). Slotted plate of a Rockler 6 in x 5/8 in Heavy Duty Wrought Steel Bed Rail Fastener (item 28597): steel, 151 x 15.9 x 3.6 mm, flush in the post's face, centred on x 0.300, from 42 to 193 mm up; two slots 6.35 mm wide and 25.4 mm tall (lower 69 to 95 mm up, upper 152 to 177 mm up), each with a hook mortise behind it 6.35 mm wide and 12.7 mm deep reaching 13 mm below the slot. Side rail: poplar, 25.4 mm thick, 165 mm tall, 2.03 m long, 3.8 kg, shown cropped 0.62 m from its near end (its weight is set so the near end carries half the rail, 18.6 N, as the whole rail's does). The fastener's hook plate (steel, 151 x 15.9 x 3.6 mm) is flush in the rail's end, centred; its two steel hooks are 4.0 mm thick, stand 11.1 mm out of the end and are 22.2 mm tall (a 12.7 mm neck and a 9.5 mm tip hanging below it, 4.0 mm clear of the end at the neck), their tops 129.5 and 46.9 mm above the rail's underside (82.5 mm apart). Seated, the rail is level, its underside 35 mm up, its end against the post's face and the hooks' necks on the slots' bottoms. Footboard end (stand-in for the footboard and the rest of the rail): a dark steel cradle on the floor at y -0.50, a 20 mm round bar across under the rail with its top 35 mm up, between two cheeks 6 mm thick, 20 mm long and 85 mm tall, 1.5 mm clear of the rail each side, and an end stop 25 mm beyond the rail's cut end (at y -0.603). Start: the rail lies on the bar and its near end's underside rests on the floor with its end 30 mm short of the post's face and 25 mm towards the arms (end's underside centre at x 0.275, y 0.040), so it slopes 3.7 degrees down to the floor and is turned 2.7 degrees. Distractors, loose on the floor, which scoring ignores: a ceramic coffee mug (114 x 90 x 80 mm, 0.30 kg) at x 0.52, y 0.40; a Phillips screwdriver (188 mm, 0.10 kg) at x 0.60, y -0.27; the assembly booklet (229 x 170 x 10 mm, 0.12 kg) at x 0.70, y 0.27. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read at each of the two hooks: s, the rail end's height above its seated line (marked on the post at setup with the rail fully seated); gap, the rail's end face to the post's face at that hook's height; e, the hook's sideways offset from its slot's centre. A hook is in when its gap is 7.5 mm or less, s is 9.5 mm or less and e at most 3.2 mm either way: it has then passed through its slot and dropped behind the plate. 0 if at any time the rail end is dropped (it falls faster than 0.5 m/s, about a 1.3 cm free fall, while every point of both grippers is more than 2 cm from the rail) or forced into the post (its end 1.5 mm or more past the post's face, a hook in its slot 1.5 mm or more below its seated height, or a hook 1.5 mm or more past the post's face more than 2.7 mm off its slot's centre, that is, pushed into the plate). Otherwise: 1.0 (success) when both hooks are seated (s and gap each 1 mm or less at both) for 3 s running, with every point of both grippers at least 3 cm from the rail and the rail still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s); else at the end 0.75 if both hooks are in with s 4.5 mm or less at both (hung on the wedge fit but not driven home); 0.5 if both hooks are in; 0.25 if one hook is in; 0 otherwise. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lift the rail's near end straight up about 15 mm to free the hooks, draw it back from the post and set its end on the floor at its tape marks (end 30 mm short of the post, 25 mm towards the robot). The wedged hooks need a firm upward pull or a tap from below to release.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. Rail cropped at 0.62 m on a cradle standing for the footboard, with the whole rail's mass and its near-end load. Hooks and slots are real-size convex colliders; the hooks' wedge fit over the last 3 mm is a stop under each hook that gives only to more than 16 N (estimated), not a modelled interference. Wood grain, rail twist and the footboard's own movement are not modelled; friction is uniform per part (rail 0.6, post 0.4, cradle 0.3).
